target.title: feat(cua): add experimental read-only diagnostics provider
target.body:
## Summary

Adds an experimental CUA provider for read-only diagnostics and existing-sandbox inventory.

The provider is intentionally registered as service control, not delegated execution. It supports:

- `crabbox doctor --provider cua`
- `crabbox list --provider cua`
- `crabbox status --provider cua --id <existing-sandbox-id>`
- trusted local configuration, environment-only credentials, provider metadata, documentation, and a non-mutating smoke test

All remote lifecycle mutation fails closed before the CUA SDK can perform it. Create, warmup, run, stop, cleanup, and bridge deletion are disabled.

## Safety gate

The pinned upstream create API has no idempotency key or client-assigned identity echoed by create, list, and get. A create that succeeds server-side but times out client-side can therefore leave a billed sandbox that Crabbox cannot identify safely.

Deletion is also disabled because the current API cannot atomically bind deletion to an immutable sandbox identity; verify-then-delete by mutable name has a replacement race.

Tracking: https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/381

## Verification

- `go build ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `go test ./internal/providers/cua/... ./internal/cli/ -run 'CUA|Provider|Registry' -count=1`
- `go test ./internal/providers/cua/... ./internal/providers/all -count=1`
- `node --test scripts/live-cua-smoke.test.js`
- `scripts/live-cua-smoke.sh`
- `node scripts/check-provider-matrix.mjs`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings

Merge remains pending a maintainer nod.

target.title: feat(fal): add SSH lease provider
target.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/694

## Summary

Adds a direct fal Compute SSH lease provider with Crabbox-managed SSH and sync support, local-claim-owned cleanup, and the `fal-ai` alias.

This also adds fal provider docs, provider matrix metadata, benchmark category generation, and an opt-in guarded live smoke script that defaults to no live provider mutation unless `CRABBOX_LIVE=1` and fal is selected.

## Lifecycle safety

- Uses the fal Compute `Idempotency-Key` header with the Crabbox lease ID for creates.
- Fsyncs the SSH keypair, exact create-request binding, and pre-mutation intent before any paid provider call; an untouched intent can be cancelled without creating a resource.
- Durably syncs every guarded claim publication and removal, including newly created state-directory ancestors, before treating ownership transitions as complete.
- Holds a cross-process acquisition-lifetime lock through ready publication and marks participating claims durably; cleanup retains unmarked legacy transitional claims rather than mistaking an older live acquisition for an abandoned one.
- Publishes a unique in-flight claim revision for every same-key POST and atomically records a known ID, retains an indeterminate outcome, or removes a first-attempt rejection.
- Bounds ambiguous-create replay to fal's documented idempotency window and treats rate limits as explicit rejections.
- Applies that bound as an actual request deadline in both immediate and stop-time replay, preserving a safety margin before provider idempotency expiry.
- Persists a cleanup-only provisional claim immediately after a provider ID is known, before readiness or SSH setup.
- Binds claims to the canonical API endpoint and a one-way credential fingerprint; lifecycle calls fail closed after endpoint or account changes.
- Serializes destructive actions under compare-and-swap claim locks, including mixed-credential cleanup.
- Serializes same-lease mutations and fal slug allocation across processes, including final ready publication and rollback claim recovery.
- Serializes ambiguous-create recovery, winner adoption, and persistence-failure cleanup so concurrent stops cannot delete the winning instance or orphan a known billable instance.
- If a provisional claim disappears mid-acquire, proves account-wide absence or reclaims/deletes the exact in-memory instance under an expected-absent claim lock; ambiguous cleanup recreates the known-ID recovery claim.
- Reconciles ambiguous unclaimed creates against complete paginated provider inventory without deleting resources Crabbox cannot prove it owns.
- Requires the documented complete fal inventory envelope before accepting a zero-resource proof, and polls raw provider inventory back to the pre-create fingerprint after stop.
- Rolls back callback/readiness/bootstrap failures unless `--keep` explicitly owns a failed-acquire recovery claim.
- Cleanup removes provider-absent local claims before TTL filtering and only deletes local-claim-owned fal instances.
- Persists delete-attempt and delete-accepted states, never replays an accepted DELETE, and requires exact `GET 404` plus complete inventory omission plus a second exact `GET 404` before removing the key and claim.
- Rejects cross-origin bearer redirects, method-rewriting mutation redirects, escaped API base paths, unsafe SSH login names, and unbounded provider requests before any credential-bearing mutation or SSH invocation.
- Redacts structured, unstructured, status, and transport error text without exposing the original secret-bearing transport cause.
- Classifies fal Compute credit and automatic-top-up rejections as `billing_blocked`, with regression coverage, instead of reporting them as generic validation failures.

## Verification

- Exact candidate: `7ca599c661eaa4115ad02597677df9f1cf94f169`
- Integrated `main` through `e25ae4ea71bfd3206b777d9ba56b5ddf0f1ea21a`.
- The current Unreleased changelog entry was added by maintainer commit `2c882a8b717eb2c8c47cea0ed5df9e880e6be336` and thanks @coygeek. The final maintainer repair commit preserves contributor credit with a `Co-authored-by` trailer.
- `go vet ./...`; `go test -race ./...`; multi-module tests; dead-code scan with zero findings; core coverage 90.2%; trimpath CLI build.
- Worker formatting, lint, typecheck, tests, and build: 934 passed, 3 skipped.
- Fal live-smoke contract suite: 68 passed.
- Docs: 54 command docs, 75 providers, 215 Markdown files/links, docs-site build.
- Cross-compiles: Darwin, Linux, and Windows on amd64 and arm64. Apple VM compatibility: 8/8 plus helper/provider race, Swift daemon, and embedded-payload checks.
- AutoReview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings. Independent lifecycle, durability, upgrade, and marker-propagation audits: clean.
- Exact-head hosted checks: [CI 7/7](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29073903741) and [Connector E2E 5/5](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29073903768).
- Exact-head Blacksmith proof: [run 29074725463](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/actions/runs/29074725463), provider `blacksmith-testbox`, lease `tbx_01kx5cdrm310z1n0advga9q4xm`. The delegated command exited 0 after asserting the exact SHA and clean diff, passing Fal race in 15.322s and CLI race in 291.895s, and building the CLI. Crabbox then stopped the successful one-shot lease, so the provider-owned Actions wrapper may show its `Run Testbox` step as cancelled during teardown. Exact post-run inventory contains none of the final or diagnostic proof leases.

The exact candidate also fixes the default 1x H100 create path: it no longer sends the 8x-only `sector` field, even when stale configuration supplies one.

## Authenticated live gate

- Authenticated fal Compute `doctor` and inventory listing passed with a temporary admin-scoped test key.
- The prior live candidate reached create authorization, then fal rejected the request before resource creation because the account did not satisfy its required $500 Compute balance and automatic-top-up threshold.
- The smoke classified that response as `billing_blocked`; exact post-attempt inventory was empty, so no funded resource or lease residue exists.
- All temporary test keys were revoked after the proof.
- The current exact head has not performed a funded create; the control plane still requires the same account balance/top-up threshold.

Keep this pull request unmerged until the exact candidate completes real create, SSH/use, destroy, and zero-residue proof, or that item-specific funded-provider gate is explicitly waived.

target.title: feat(providers): add local Lume macOS leases
target.body:
## Summary

- add a native `lume` SSH-lease provider for local Apple-silicon macOS VMs
- clone one stopped golden image into one isolated VM per Crabbox lease
- rotate SSH host keys on first clone boot, pin a per-lease host identity, and inject only a unique public key
- serialize acquisition and enforce Apple's two-running-macOS-guest host limit
- identity-fence the detached `lume run` owner, work around Lume 0.3.16 stop/readiness defects, and verify stop/delete before claim cleanup
- add claim-safe release and multi-storage cleanup, trusted configuration, ARM64 target validation, docs, metadata, and live-smoke dispatch
- add reusable macOS image hooks for first-boot identity and optional Cua Driver startup, plus noninteractive developer-tool setup improvements

## Why

Crabbox needs a local macOS backend that can reuse layered Lume images without baking credentials into them. Each session should have its own VM, filesystem, machine identity, SSH key, and host-key trust while still supporting normal Crabbox sync/run/release behavior.

This is separate from #678, which adds a cloud Linux CUA provider; this PR covers local macOS VMs on user-owned Apple-silicon infrastructure.

## Validation

- `go test -race ./internal/providers/lume ./internal/providers/all -count=1`
- `go vet ./internal/providers/lume ./internal/providers/all`
- full `go test ./internal/cli -count=1`
- Windows ARM64 cross-compilation of the Lume provider
- docs, provider-matrix, shell syntax, plist, and Node live-smoke checks
- real Apple-silicon lifecycle with two concurrent leases from the same stopped golden image:
  - distinct VM names, IPs, platform UUIDs, SSH keypairs, and ED25519 host-key fingerprints
  - independent Crabbox commands at the same guest path
  - Cua Accessibility, Screen Recording, and actual desktop capture passed in both VMs
  - Tailscale remained installed but logged out with `NeedsLogin` in both VMs
  - concurrent release left no VM, owner process, claim, key, known-hosts, private log, or temporary password-helper residue

## Current boundaries

- macOS/ARM64 only; Lume is not used for Windows or Linux guests
- the prepared guest currently needs Lume's default bootstrap account/password; custom bootstrap passwords are not yet supported
- desktop/webVNC bridging and Crabbox-managed Tailscale enrollment are intentionally not advertised yet
- reusable image layers remain credential-free; credentials are injected only into disposable clones after boot

target.title: feat: validate required run artifacts against a schema (`--require-artifact-schema`)
target.body:
Closes #1070 

---

## Summary

Adds a post-run evidence gate that validates a required artifact's **JSON content** against a declared schema, not just its existence. Today `--require-artifact` is — per `docs/features/artifacts.md` — *"an existence guard, not manifest validation"*, so a run passes its proof gate even when the proof file is empty, truncated, or missing the fields that make it evidence. `--require-artifact-schema remote=schema.json` closes that gap: present → **valid**.

```sh
crabbox run \
  --require-artifact-schema docs/metrics/hermetic-agents-e2e.json=schemas/hermetic.schema.json \
  -- ./scripts/run_hermetic_agents_demo.sh
```

Missing, unparseable, or non-conforming → `exit 7` with the exact violations listed. Malformed schema file → `exit 2` at preflight.

## Motivation

Directly addresses the gap named in `docs/features/hermetic-agent-evidence.md`: *"Crabbox can require that the proof file exists; it does not validate the proof schema."* Strengthens the hermetic-agent, test-result, and manifest evidence flows for a tool whose contract is reproducible, reviewable run evidence.

## What changed

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/cli/run_artifact_schema.go` | **New.** Dependency-free JSON-Schema-subset validator, the `remote=schema.json` spec parser + preflight loader, and the SSH fetch/validate gate helper. |
| `internal/cli/run_artifact_schema_test.go` | **New.** Table-driven unit tests for the validator, spec parser, and loader. |
| `internal/cli/run.go` | Flag registration, preflight load, `--sync-only` rejection, delegated-provider guard, the post-run gate hook, and evidence attachment. |
| `internal/cli/timing.go` | New `TimingReport.SchemaValidations` field (`omitempty`). |
| `docs/features/artifacts.md` | Documents the new flag next to the existence-guard note. |

Net: most of the change is the new validator (~380 lines) and its tests
(~335 lines, including fail-closed, byte-cap, and injected-reader gate coverage);
the wiring in `run.go` is +26 lines.

## Design decisions

- **Zero new dependency, fail-closed.** The schema language is a small subset of
  JSON Schema (`type`, `required`, `properties`, `items`, `enum`). Parsing is
  **fail-closed** via `json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields`: any unsupported
  validation keyword (`pattern`, `minimum`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`,
  `$ref`, …) is rejected at preflight with `exit 2`, at every nesting level, so a
  passing gate always means the supplied constraints were actually enforced.
  Only annotation keywords (`$schema`, `$id`, `title`, `description`, `$comment`,
  `examples`, `default`, `deprecated`) are accepted and ignored. The subset can
  be widened deliberately later.
- **Validation is local, and bounded.** Artifact bytes are read into memory via
  the existing `runSSHOutput` base64 transport (never written to the working
  tree), and the read is **capped at 5 MiB** — the remote command reads one byte
  past the limit (`head -c` / a bounded PowerShell read) and the decoder rejects
  anything larger, so an oversized or runaway artifact fails the gate instead of
  flooding SSH output and exhausting local memory. Keeping validation in Go makes
  it provider-agnostic and unit-testable.
- **Mirrors the existing gate.** Runs after command success alongside
  `--require-artifact`, reuses its `exit 7` gate class and safe-path validation
  (`validateRequiredRunArtifactGlobs`), and follows the `stringListFlag` pattern.
- **Distinct error taxonomy.** Command failure keeps its own exit code; malformed
  schema → `exit 2` (preflight); missing/unfetchable or non-conforming artifact
  → `exit 7`.
- **SSH-backed first.** Delegated-run providers reject the flag at preflight
  (`exit 2`), mirroring how `--require-artifact` collection and other artifact
  features are already gated behind an explicit delegated capability. Delegated
  support is a follow-up.

## Evidence schema

```json
{
  "schemaValidations": [
    {
      "artifact": "docs/metrics/hermetic-agents-e2e.json",
      "schema": "schemas/hermetic.schema.json",
      "valid": false,
      "violations": [
        "qa_verdict: missing required property \"qa_verdict\"",
        "count: expected type number, got string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`omitempty`, so timing JSON is byte-identical when the flag is unused.

## Testing / verification

The valuable core — `validateJSONAgainstSchema`, `parseArtifactSchema`, the spec parser, and the loader — is pure stdlib with no lease/network/provider dependency. It is covered by table-driven tests:

- valid document → no violations; missing required / wrong type / `enum` mismatch → violation at the right path;
- nested object and `items[i]` index paths reported correctly;
- non-JSON and empty documents → a single `json` violation, not a crash;
- type mismatch does not cascade into child violations;
- malformed schema → `exit 2` (distinct from `exit 7`);
- **fail-closed:** `pattern`, `minimum`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf`, `$ref`, and a nested unsupported keyword are each rejected at preflight; annotation keywords are accepted;
- **bounded fetch:** `decodeBoundedBase64` rejects oversized payloads and the remote command carries the `head -c` byte bound;
- **gate behaviour (via an injected reader, no live SSH):** valid → pass, invalid content → `exit 7` with violations, fetch error → `exit 7`, oversized → `exit 7` — asserting results, ordering, and exit codes;
- spec parsing: valid `remote=schema.json`, missing `=`, unsafe/absolute/`..` remote path; missing, malformed, and duplicate specs → `exit 2`.

**Verified locally:** the validator, spec/loader, byte-cap, and gate logic were extracted verbatim into a standalone module and run with `go test` — all tests pass, `go vet` clean.

> **Note for CI:** this development environment cannot compile the full
> `internal/cli` package because the repo pins future-dated modules
> (`google.golang.org/api@v0.282.0`, `genproto@…20260526…`) that the public
> `proxy.golang.org` returns `403` for (they resolve only via the private
> proxy). The gate's ordering, exit codes, and evidence are now covered by
> injected-reader unit tests, so what remains unverified locally is specifically
> the live SSH transport and full-package integration — a redacted live
> transcript (valid / invalid / missing / oversized / malformed-schema) should be
> attached from CI or a real SSH-backed lease. Run:

```sh
gofmt -l $(git ls-files '*.go')
go vet ./...
go build -trimpath -o bin/crabbox ./cmd/crabbox
go test -race ./internal/cli/
```

## Non-goals / follow-ups

- Not a data-safety / secrets scanner (stays a separate concern).
- Not remote validation; not a JUnit/`results` replacement.
- Widening the supported keyword subset, making the 5 MiB cap configurable, and a delegated-provider capability contract are documented follow-ups.

## Addressing review (ClawSweeper / Codex, blocked → resolved)

- **[P2] Unbounded remote read → resource exhaustion.** Fixed. The fetch is now
  capped at 5 MiB: `remoteBoundedReadBase64Command` reads `maxBytes+1` bytes and
  `decodeBoundedBase64` rejects anything over the limit, with oversized-path unit
  tests. (`internal/cli/run_artifact_schema.go`)
- **[P2] Silently ignoring unsupported schema keywords → false proof.** Fixed by
  making parsing fail-closed (`DisallowUnknownFields`) and rejecting unsupported
  validation keywords at preflight, with tests for `pattern` / `minimum` /
  `additionalProperties` / `anyOf` / `$ref`. Docs no longer claim general JSON
  Schema compatibility. This adopts the reviewer's recommended
  **"fail closed on keywords"** contract.
- **Real behaviour proof.** Gate ordering, exit codes, and evidence are now
  exercised by injected-reader unit tests. A live SSH/CLI transcript still needs
  to come from CI or a real lease, because this environment cannot build the full
  `internal/cli` package (private future-dated modules; see the CI note above) —
  not because the gate logic is unverified.

Closes the schema-validation gap tracked in `docs/features/hermetic-agent-evidence.md`.
